back_en: Find a comfortable position, sitting or lying down.
Take three deep breaths. Let the exhale be slower than the inhale.
On the third exhale, let your eyes close.
Let your shoulders relax.
Try to sit still, if you can.
Let everything be as it is.

flags.reason: reads like translated 'let everything be as it is'

back_en: Feel how the weight of the body presses down. Feel your feet on the floor.
Feel the weight of your hands, and then your whole arms, how they lie where they lie.
Notice how the body feels right now. It might be tired, restless, or calm.
Now let's move attention through the body, part by part, starting from the feet.
Sink into your feet and settle into them. Feel deep contact with your feet.

flags.reason: 'settle into your feet' translated yoga phrasing

back_en: Feel the space inside your feet. Feel that you are this space itself.
Let the breath settle down there, together with you, so the inhale doesn't lift you back up.
Now rise into your legs and settle into them. Feel the space inside your legs.
Now move into the pelvis. Feel that you are inside the pelvis.
Now rise into your belly and settle into it. Feel that you are the inner space of the belly itself.

flags.reason: 'settle into' + 'you are the space' pattern reads translated

back_en: Now rise into your chest. Make yourself at home inside the chest, as if sitting in your own heart.
Now settle into your arms and hands, all the way to the fingertips.
Now move into your neck. Feel that you are inside the neck.
Now rise into your head. Let your forehead and eyes soften.
Now settle into the whole body at once. Feel: this is your body.
Now direct your attention to the breath. Breathe as usual.
Feel where the breath is most noticeable. Nose, chest, or belly.
Track one inhale, then one exhale.
When you notice thoughts have carried you off, just return to the breath.
Feel the whole inhale and exhale, entirely: from the first instant of the inhale, through the pause between them, to the last instant of the exhale.

flags.reason: one continuous descriptive clause, hard in one breath

back_en: Doesn't matter how long the thoughts carried you off. Start again with the next inhale.
If you're somewhere else right now, that's fine. Return to the breath.
Now let go of the breath. No need to watch it anymore. Let the mind rest as it is.
Sounds will reach you on their own. No need to listen closely. Let them come and go.
Thoughts will come the same way. No need to stop them.
When you notice a thought has pulled you in, look at what's happening to it. Where does it go? Then start again, no matter how long you were gone.
If there's some feeling in you right now, find where it lives in your face and body. Just look at it.
Now return to the body. Feel how you're sitting here, in the room.

flags.reason: assumes sitting though intro allowed lying too

back_en: When you're ready, slowly open your eyes.
First let's wake up the body with light stretching. A couple of simple movements is enough for the whole day to feel different.
Sit up straight, closer to the edge of the chair, feet flat on the floor. Do everything very slowly and skip any movement that causes pain.
Stretch both arms up toward the ceiling. Hold them there, exhale, and let your breathing return to normal.
Lower your arms, and now roll your shoulders up, back, and down. Wide and slow, several times.
Tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder, face forward. Keep both shoulders down and let the weight of your head do the work.
Now tilt your left ear toward your left shoulder. Let the same weight do the work.
Turn your head and look over your right shoulder, torso facing forward. Keep your chin level, turn only as far as feels easy.
Now look over your left shoulder the same way. Keep your chin level.
Extend both arms forward at chest height, palms facing each other. Reach forward with them and round your upper back.
Lower your arms, now clasp your hands behind your back, arms straight. Lift your chest and open your shoulders.
Unclasp your hands and stretch them upward. Grab your right wrist with your left hand, lean left, and feel your right side stretch.
Now grab your left wrist with your right hand. Lean right and feel your left side stretch.
Lower your arms and place your palms on your lower back, fingers pointing down. Gently arch back and look up slightly, only as far as feels easy.
Return upright. Place your left palm on the outside of your right knee and use it to turn your torso to the right, pelvis facing forward.
Now place your right palm on the outside of your left knee and turn your torso to the left. Pelvis stays facing forward.
Place your right ankle on your left knee. Sit up straight and lean forward slightly until you feel a stretch along the outside of your right thigh.
Now place your left ankle on your right knee. Lean forward slightly until you feel a stretch along the outside of your left thigh.
Take your leg off your knee, both feet flat on the floor. Toes stay on the floor, lift both heels to rise onto your toes, then slowly lower. Several times.
I will do whatever it takes to grow as a person.

flags.reason: 'вырасти как человек' reads translated 'grow as a person'

back_en: Now let's breathe through the heart, to calm the body and mind together. Direct your attention to the center of your chest and imagine the breath entering and leaving through that point.
While you breathe, let's raise up gratitude. Recall something small that happened recently that you're grateful for, like a friend's smile or sun on your skin.
Feel gratitude in your chest.
Now think about something you rarely appreciate.
Feel this gratitude as you breathe.
Now think of someone you're grateful to.
Feel this in your chest as you breathe.
If it fades, bring it back.
Let it spread through your body.
This is a skill. Each time, the heart and mind learn to calm down together faster.
Now let's do a short breathing technique that quickly calms the body. Two inhales through the nose, then one long exhale through the mouth.
Inhale through the nose, and at the peak take in a little more air. Then slowly release it all through the mouth, for as long as you can.
If you get dizzy, breathe normally for a bit, then continue.
At the peak, take in a little more air.
For as long as you can.
At your own pace.
The danger has passed.

flags.reason: unclear referent for 'danger' without prior context

back_en: Now let's bring attention out of the head into the room, to slow a mind that's sped up.
Open your eyes if they're closed. Find three things you see, and name them to yourself, one by one.
Now listen. Find two sounds, near or far, and let them reach you.
Now feel. Find one thing your body is touching: the chair, the floor, your own hands, and just notice it.

flags.reason: 'одно, чего касается тело' is stilted word order

back_en: When you notice you've been pulled back into the story, return to what you see, hear, and feel right now.
Take one slow exhale, longer than the inhale.
Notice that the room is the same as it was a minute ago. It's you who slowed down.
First let's cool the body down, because the mind won't cool down before the body does.
Unclench your jaw. Drop your shoulders. Open your palms.
Now silently ask yourself what you need right now, not what they deserve.
Now let's set one intention for the next block of work, so you enter it mindfully. One thing, not a list.
Silently name the first action you'll take when this is over, small enough to start within a minute.
See yourself doing it: where you're sitting and what's in front of you.
When you feel the urge to check something else — and you will — that's your signal to return to the one task.
Take one slow inhale and let the rest of the day wait outside this block.
Now let's set the day: choose one thing that will make today not wasted. One thing, not a list.
Silently name it. Then name the first small step toward it.
See yourself in the evening, when that step is already done. Notice how it feels in the body.
Hold this feeling for a few breaths. This is what you enter the day with.
If the day goes sideways — and it happens — that one step is still yours.
Now let's rehearse the beginning — that's exactly what the nerves latch onto, which is why we train it.
See the room or screen as they will be. See the person or people in front of you.
Now watch yourself begin: saying the first phrase in your own voice, calmly and unhurried.
Feel how your body sits or stands when everything's going well. Take that posture right now.
Whatever happens after the start, you've already done the hardest part.
Take one slow exhale and let your shoulders drop.
Now we repair, not punish. A slip is information, and shame is exactly what leads to the next one.
Place your palm on your chest. Say to yourself: this is hard, and I'm not the only one it's hard for.
Now find the moment right before it happened, not to judge, just to see. That's exactly where you'll catch it next time.
Say to yourself: may I be kind to myself. May I try again.
Take a slow inhale and a longer exhale. Nothing else needs to happen right now.
You noticed. Everything else rests on this skill, and you just used it.
Now let's let the body rest. Falling asleep isn't required, and not sleeping isn't required either.
Let the body grow heavy. Feel how the bed or floor holds your weight.
Release your jaw, open your palms. Let your eyes rest.
Now just rest here, for as long as this lasts.
If thoughts come, let them pass. No need to follow them.
Let each exhale take you a bit deeper.
When the time comes, wiggle your fingers and toes and let your eyes slowly open.
Now let's gently wake the body. You don't need energy to begin — it appears from the beginning itself.
Now let's step out of the loop. You can't stop thoughts, but you can stop feeding them.
Every time you notice you're in the loop again, say to yourself: 'thinking,' and return to the breath. That one word is the whole technique.
This is the long version. This time you'll find more.

flags.reason: 'you'll find more' is vague without list context

back_en: Go slowly, so you have time to feel gratitude for each one.
You can also recall the bad things that aren't happening to you.
When thoughts return to anxiety, that's your signal. Find one more.
Now let's close out the workday, so it doesn't keep running in the background tonight.
Silently name the first thing you'll do tomorrow, one step, and leave it there until morning.
Say to yourself: work is done for today.
Let your shoulders drop. Let your hands go still.
